PTFE Gaskets · Sealing

PTFE Gaskets & Rings

Flange gaskets, envelope gaskets and precision-cut rings in PTFE (Teflon) — cut to standard pipe sizes or to your own bolt pattern for chemical, pharmaceutical and process plant.

Request a Quote WhatsApp

A PTFE gasket seals joints that carry media most other gasket materials cannot survive — strong acids, alkalis, solvents and oxidisers. As a PTFE gasket manufacturer, SK Polymers cuts rings, flange gaskets and envelope gaskets to standard dimensions or to your drawing. The right choice depends on the flange, the bolt load available and the media.

Types of PTFE gasket

“PTFE gasket” covers several constructions that behave quite differently once bolted up:

General guidance. Confirm the gasket type for your flange, media, temperature and pressure.
TypeConstructionStrengthsWatch-outs
Solid virgin PTFECut from skived or moulded virgin sheetWidest chemical resistance; clean, non-contaminatingCreeps (cold-flows) under bolt load, so bolt stress can relax over time
Filled PTFECut from glass-, carbon- or other filled sheetMuch better creep resistance than virgin; holds bolt load betterFiller limits some chemistry — e.g. glass with hydrofluoric acid
Expanded PTFE (ePTFE)Soft, microporous PTFE sheet or tapeVery conformable; seals uneven, warped or damaged flange facesCompresses a lot — thickness and bolting need care
Envelope gasketPTFE jacket over a compressible insertPTFE wetted face with the resilience of the insert; low seating stressThe insert must suit the temperature; only the jacket is chemically resistant

Our PTFE gasket selection guide walks through how to choose between them.

PTFE envelope gaskets

An envelope gasket wraps a thin PTFE jacket around a compressible insert, such as a compressed fibre sheet or an elastomer. The media only touches PTFE, while the insert provides the springiness that solid PTFE lacks. Because envelope gaskets seal at modest bolt loads, they are a common choice for glass-lined, ceramic and other fragile flanges that cannot be tightened hard.

Flange gaskets: full face or inside bolt circle

A full-face gasket covers the whole flange face and has bolt holes punched through it; it is common on flat-faced and non-metallic flanges. An inside-bolt-circle (IBC) or ring gasket sits inside the bolts and is located by them; it is typical on raised-face flanges. We cut both to standard pipe tables or to your bolt pattern — tell us if you need dimensions to ASME B16.21 or EN 1514-1.

Choosing a grade

Virgin PTFE is the safe choice for aggressive or high-purity media, but on its own it relaxes under bolt load. Filled grades resist this cold flow and are usually preferred on metal flanges with steady bolting. Expanded PTFE and envelope constructions solve a different problem — flanges that are uneven or too fragile for high bolt stress. If you are unsure, see virgin vs filled PTFE or simply describe the joint and we will suggest an option.

Applications

  • Pipe flange sealing — chemical, pharmaceutical, food and process pipework.
  • Pump and valve bodies — body, cover and bonnet joints handling corrosive media.
  • Heat-exchanger covers — channel and cover gaskets where the process stream is aggressive.
  • Manhole and vessel covers — large-diameter gaskets for reactors, tanks and glass-lined vessels.
  • Washers and spacers — insulating or chemically resistant washers cut from PTFE sheet.

Supply and customisation

  • Rings and washers
  • Flange gaskets to pipe tables
  • Custom bolt-hole patterns
  • Full-face or inside bolt circle
  • Envelope gaskets
  • Thickness to suit

Available sizes and thicknesses depend on gasket type and grade — send your flange details or drawing and we will confirm what we can supply.

Installation notes

PTFE gaskets reward careful installation. Flange faces should be clean, undamaged and parallel; bolts should be tightened gradually in a cross pattern to an even load; and, as a rule, the thinnest gasket that can accommodate the flange surface finish relaxes least under load. Because PTFE creeps and expands with temperature, follow your site’s bolting procedure for checking joints after the first heat cycle. Details on PTFE behaviour are in the PTFE properties guide.

What to include in your enquiry

  1. Gasket type — solid, filled, expanded or envelope — or the joint details so we can suggest one.
  2. Pipe size and pressure class with the standard, or OD, ID, PCD and bolt-hole size and number.
  3. Full-face or inside bolt circle, and the thickness.
  4. Media, temperature and pressure.
  5. Quantity, and whether this is a one-off or repeat order.

Common Questions

PTFE Gasket FAQs

Questions buyers commonly ask before ordering PTFE gaskets.

Ask a Question

Teflon™ is a Chemours brand name for PTFE, and “Teflon gasket” is widely used to mean a PTFE gasket. We supply PTFE gaskets; we do not claim they are the branded product.

Virgin PTFE creeps, or cold-flows, under sustained compression, so the gasket thins slightly and bolt stress relaxes. Filled PTFE, expanded PTFE and envelope gaskets are common ways to reduce the effect.

Envelope gaskets suit glass-lined, ceramic and other fragile flanges, and joints where you want a PTFE wetted face but need more resilience than solid PTFE. Check that the insert material suits your temperature.

Yes. Send the OD, ID, pitch circle diameter, bolt-hole size and number — or a drawing — and we will cut gaskets to suit, either full-face or inside the bolt circle.

Expanded PTFE is very conformable and fills uneven or slightly damaged faces well. Our gasket selection guide compares the options.
